body.statement: Let \(\mathsf A\) and \(\mathsf B\) be compact metric spaces, let \(\alpha\in\mathcal P(\mathsf A)\) and \(\beta\in\mathcal P(\mathsf B)\), and let \(\mathcal R\subseteq\mathsf A\times\mathsf B\) be closed.  There exists a coupling \(\pi\in\Gamma(\alpha,\beta)\) with \(\pi(\mathcal R)=1\) if and only if \(\alpha(A)\leq\beta(\mathcal R(A))\) for every compact \(A\subseteq\mathsf A\), where \(\mathcal R(A)=\{b\in\mathsf B:(a,b)\in\mathcal R\text{ for some }a\in A\}\).

source.locator: Theorem 7, closed-relation criterion for a probability measure with prescribed marginals
source.verbatim_statement: For any ε ≥ 0 and any closed set K ⊂ S × S, there exists a probability measure λ with marginals μ and ν such that λ(K) ≥ 1 − ε if and only if ν(F) ≤ μ(π₁(K ∩ (S × F))) + ε, ∀ F ∈ C.

upstream.citation: V. Strassen (1965), The existence of probability measures with given marginals

attestation.note: Exact accessible restatement verified in Kamihigashi and Stachurski, Partial Stochastic Dominance, IPAG Working Paper 2014-403, p. 20, Theorem 7.1, retrieved 2026-09-14; that theorem explicitly attributes the result to Strassen (1965).
